Rumors indicate the AirPods 5 will be released next week alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the iPhone Ultra. Here's what we know so far about the new AirPods.

The AirPods 5 are expected to debut at the September 9 event in two models, but without a camera

Apple's most important annual event will be held next week on September 9. In addition to a lineup of new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and possibly home products, the AirPods 5 is also expected to make an appearance.

The AirPods 4 launched in 2024. Looking back at history, Apple typically spaces each generation of AirPods two to three years apart. AirPods debuted in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. So based on this timeline, launching a new model this year roughly fits the established pattern.

However, surprisingly, there have been very few rumors and leaks about the new AirPods so far.

Most recent AirPods rumors have revolved around a new model equipped with a camera. A video leaked from Apple software first showed the camera-equipped version in action, leading to speculation that this new model could debut soon.

However, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman noted that AirPods with a camera won't arrive until 2027. But he expects the AirPods 5 without a camera to make its debut at Apple's September event. He recently wrote:

Gurman added in a post on social platform X that the AirPods 5 will come in two distinctly different models:

  • Equipped with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC)
  • Without ANC

In previous reports, Gurman mentioned that he expects the AirPods 5 will not include the heart rate sensor found in the AirPods Pro 3, but Apple is "researching adding more health features to AirPods incrementally, including a body temperature sensor." He also mentioned separately that Apple is developing an "H3 chip aimed at further reducing latency and improving sound quality."

Whether the AirPods 5 will ultimately use the H3 chip remains unknown. When Apple introduced the H2 chip, it was initially exclusive to the AirPods Pro lineup.

However, new health sensors could potentially be included in the AirPods 5, and the H3 chip is also a possible option. Beyond that, details about the AirPods 5 remain quite limited. Or, much like when Apple launched the AirPods Max 2 earlier this year, they could still surprise everyone when they unveil the AirPods 5.

What features do you want Apple to include in the next-generation AirPods? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
